Method of Attack: HVACKer: malware interacts with computer thermal sensors to read temperature variations caused by HVAC systems and convert them into binary code to send commands to malware inside air-gapped networks
Stuxnet, Gauss, Flame: malware used to infect highly secure networks via infected USB devices
LED-it-Go: exfiltrate data from air-gapped systems via HDD's activity LED
LEDSPEAKE: use headphones to record audio and spy on nearby users
9-1-1 DDoS: launch DDoS attacks that can cripple emergency systems
USBee: make a USB connector's data bus emit electromagnetic emissions to exfiltrate data
AirHopper: use local GPU card to emit electromagnetic signals to nearby mobile phones to steal data
Fansmitter: steal data from air-gapped PCs using sounds from GPU fan
DiskFiltration: use controlled HDD read/write operations to steal data via sound waves
BitWhisper: exfiltrate data from non-networked computers using heat emanations
xLED: use router or switch LEDs to exfiltrate data
Shattered Trust: use backdoored replacement parts to take over smartphones
aIR-Jumper: use security camera infrared capabilities to steal data from air-gapped networks
Discoverer: Researchers from the Cyber Security Research Center at the Ben-Gurion University of the Negev in Israel
Impacted Systems: Enterprise, government, and military buildings with HVAC systems
Attack Vector: HVACKer: breach and take control of Internet-connected HVAC systems or building automation software to send thermal signals
Infected USB devices to infect isolated networks
Electromagnetic emissions from USB connectors, GPU cards, and LEDs
Indicators of Compromise: Temperature variations caused by HVAC systems used to send commands
Electromagnetic emissions from USB data bus
